decisive_items: Focal, non-keratinizing invasive squamous cell carcinoma
infiltrative process at the base and root of the tongue, invading the most inferior aspects of the mouth floor
P16– INK and Cyto5/6 immunohistochemistry were positive
response.rationale: R3 provides the most specific and accurate diagnosis, combining the histopathologic finding of squamous cell carcinoma with the anatomical location (tongue) as confirmed by imaging. R1 is correct but lacks the site specification. Other candidates either misattribute the etiology (HPV, smoking) or describe symptoms rather than the diagnosis.

rejected.why: P16 negativity rules out HPV-related carcinoma; the label is incorrect.
Describes dysphagia as a symptom, not the underlying neoplastic diagnosis.
Weight loss is a nonspecific symptom, not a diagnosis.
Tongue atrophy and deviation are signs of the tumor, not the diagnosis itself.
Smoking history is a risk factor, not a diagnosis; the tumor is not attributed to smoking.
Dysphagia and oral cavity tumor are descriptive but lack the specific histopathologic diagnosis.
